question: What degree of practical commitment exactly preserves every admissible completion of a partial picking plan?
rejected_claims: Local admissibility can fail to compose: already familiar in Elga and earlier decision theory.
Mutually exclusive branches require modal coordination despite one actual choice: explicit in Huntley–Troffaes Example 6 and Pettigrew, Campbell-Moore and Konek 2025.
As-if precision is not actual precise belief: explicit in the closest 2025 source.
Common-witness algorithms are possible: established computational literature; no priority claim.
A geometric-pooling objection to Steele: abandoned without adequate main-text access.
retained_contribution: An exact distinction between obtaining some E-admissible implementation and preserving all permissible completions of a partially specified policy. A full retained witness set is sufficient; any proper nonempty closed convex restriction can lose a permissible binary-menu continuation. Thus the requirement to coordinate does not itself mandate an early point proxy.
closest_source: Pettigrew, Campbell-Moore and Konek 2025, Choosing how to choose, especially 3.2.1 and 4.2.1
relationship_to_closest_source: Accept its common-witness theorem and its explicit distinction between modal coordination and sharp belief. Develop a limited answer to its implementation question for finite partially specified plans; do not represent it as unaware of the basic distinction.
contribution_type: Philosophical refinement using elementary convex geometry and an executable counterexample search, not a novel decision rule or a counterexample to the published theorem.
remaining_risk: The retained result may be judged a modest corollary rather than a significant original contribution. Searches are bounded and do not establish absence from the literature. Source-hosted full texts of Bradley–Steele and Chandler were not read.
